text: Kim's causal exclusion argument pressures non-reductive physicalism by claiming that:
choices: If a distinct mental property causes a physical effect that already has a sufficient physical cause, the effect is systematically overdetermined — which is implausible
Mental properties cannot supervene on physical properties
Folk psychology makes no testable predictions
Zombies are conceivable and therefore metaphysically possible
explanation: Kim's worry is that, given causal closure, every physical effect already has a sufficient physical cause; a distinct (non-identical) mental cause would then make the effect overdetermined, and rejecting systematic overdetermination pushes one toward reduction or epiphenomenalism. Option 1 denies supervenience (which non-reductive physicalists accept); options 2 and 3 belong to eliminativism and the zombie argument respectively.
